properties.name: BUILT 2026-09-29 (PR #624): notes and defaults now read the merged node, and the add_verification guard kept its rule but now names the stored verdict. The guard question stays OPEN for the owner
properties.source: PR #624 (branch fix/a-revise-keeps-what-was-not-passed), dev_reflow2 hub fix program 2026-09-29
properties.statement:
What PR #624 built against this open question, so the idea is not read as settled by the code:
- DEFAULTS read the merged node (option B's half that nobody objected to). record_finding writes fact_type/basis defaults on CREATE only.
- NOTES read the merged node (option A). add_change_event's `undated` note reads the stored event.
- GUARDS were left on the call; only the refusal was changed, which is option C's shape. add_verification still refuses findings without a status on a revise. The refusal now names the verdict and run date the check already holds, so the caller re-sends knowing what is stored.

The ruling this question asks for — may new findings on a revise inherit a stored verdict (a text correction) or must they restate it (a new run)? — was NOT taken. It is still the owner's.

Pinned by crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_revise_keeps_what_it_was_not_passed.rs, whose fourth case asserts the refusal names `passing`. That case would need to change if the owner chooses B for guards.
